summary: Describes a way for a mobile node and a correspondent node to preconfigure data that can be used to precompute a Binding Management Key. That key is later used to authorize Binding Updates, which secure Mobile IPv6 route optimization. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Two friends agree on a secret handshake ahead of time. Later, when one moves, the secret proves the new address is really theirs.

subtitle: A pre-agreed secret lets a Mobile IPv6 node and its peer skip the slow routability tests when updating addresses.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv6 route optimization normally uses a periodic return routability test to authorize Binding Updates, and the test messages add latency.
tldr.mechanism: A mobile node and a correspondent node preconfigure a shared key (Kcn) and two nonces, from which the Binding Management Key (Kbm) is computed in advance, so the routability messages can be omitted.
tldr.outcome: Latency drops and the home address is verified more strongly, but it only suits small, trusted, same-administration setups because the care-of address is not verified.

today: RFC 4449 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text itself says return routability stays the default for general use.

sections.title: An Alternative to Return Routability
sections.content:
This RFC offers a low-latency alternative for protecting the signaling used in Mobile IPv6 route optimization. The default mechanism in RFC 3775 uses a periodic return routability test. It checks both the mobile node's right to use a specific home address and the validity of the claimed care-of address, and it needs no configuration beyond the mobile node's home agent.

The mechanism here requires a shared secret between the mobile node and its correspondent node. Because of that, the routability test messages can be omitted, which means significantly smaller latency. The right to use a home address is also ensured more strongly than in RFC 3775.

The price is limited applicability: preconfiguration is needed, and the validity of claimed care-of addresses is not verified, so mobile nodes must be trusted not to misbehave.
sections.eli5: Normally you prove who you are by answering a few questions every time. Here you and your friend agreed on a secret in advance, so you can skip the questions and be quicker.

sections.title: When This Mechanism Applies
sections.content:
The applicability statement lists conditions that must all be met:

  • The mobile node and correspondent node are administered within the same domain.
  • The correspondent node has good reason to trust the mobile node, and in particular is certain it will not launch flooding attacks against a third party.
  • The configuration effort is acceptable, and users MUST be able to generate or select a sufficiently good value for Kcn.
  • There is a wish for higher efficiency or greater assurance about the home address.
  • The mechanism is used only for authenticating Binding Update messages, not data, so traffic volume is low.

It can also help with software development, testing and diagnostics of mobility signaling. Typical fits are inside a corporation or between specific users. The general Internet and public network operators are typically not possible, because of the manual configuration effort and the trust that is required.
sections.eli5: A secret handshake works between a small club of people who know each other. It would not work for strangers all over the world.

sections.title: Precomputing the Binding Management Key
sections.content:
The mobile node and correspondent node preconfigure three pieces of data, associated with the mobile node's home address:

  • A shared key, Kcn, used to generate keygen tokens, at least 20 octets long.
  • A nonce for generating the care-of keygen token.
  • A nonce for generating the home keygen token.

The keygen tokens MUST be generated from Kcn and the nonces as in the Mobile IPv6 return routability procedure, and the Binding Management Key (Kbm) is then generated from the tokens in the same way as in RFC 3775. Kcn MUST be generated with sufficient randomness (see RFC 4086).

When a Binding Update is authenticated with such a precomputed Kbm, the Binding Authorization Data suboption MUST be present. The Nonce Indices option SHOULD NOT be present. If it is, the indices SHOULD be ignored and are not part of the authentication data calculation, which is performed exactly as in RFC 3775.
sections.eli5: Both sides write down the same secret code and two lucky numbers beforehand. Later each side mixes them the same way and gets the same key, with no messages needed.

sections.title: Replay Protection
sections.content:
Replay protection comes from the Sequence Number field of the Binding Update. If the correspondent node does not remember recent values, a malicious node could replay old Binding Updates and fool it into routing toward an old care-of address. So a correspondent node using a precomputable Kbm MUST keep track of the most recent Sequence Number, for example by committing it to stable storage.

The method fails if the 16 bit counter cycles (not more than 65,536 distinct uses of Kbm) or if sequence numbers are not protected against reboots. An update every hour would need new keys about every 7 years; one every minute would give protection for over a month. When the field rolls over, the parties SHOULD configure a new Kcn so that new Kbm values are computed.
sections.eli5: Each note gets a number, and the receiver remembers the latest one. If someone shows an old note again, the receiver sees the number is old and ignores it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Manually configured keys MUST be used in conformance with RFC 4107. To protect against dictionary attacks, the configured information is intended to be used ONLY for authenticating Binding Update messages.

A mobile node MUST use a different Kcn for each node in its Binding Update List, and a correspondent node MUST ensure every mobile node uses a different Kcn, so the sender of a Binding Update can always be uniquely determined. This matters because the method gives no guarantee that the care-of address is legitimate, so it SHOULD only be applied between nodes under the same administration.

Return routability remains RECOMMENDED for all general use and MUST be the default unless the user explicitly enters the preconfigured data for a peer. A node configured to use this mechanism with a peer SHOULD NOT try another mechanism even if the peer asks, to prevent bidding down attacks. No upper bound is defined on the lifetime of the precomputable Kbm.

If a correspondent node does not track sequence numbers, it could accept an old care-of address. If that address was reallocated to another IPv6 node, that node could receive unwanted traffic.
sections.eli5: Use a different secret with every friend, keep it for one job only, and fall back to the careful method by default.
